title: Adaptive On-Prem Entitlement Bundles and Controlled Upgrade Cadence Experiment
creator: Priya Desai
description: Run a controlled experiment to validate a two-part commercial construct for on-prem / VPC customers: a baseline perpetual or term license fee that covers core product entitlements plus an optional ops/maintenance subscription that controls upgrade cadence and SLA tiering. The goal is to reduce friction for enterprise procurement while giving customers explicit controls over upgrade timing and operational escalation rights.
background: Sales and Solutions teams report repeated stalls in large deals due to: unclear on-prem upgrade policy, customers demanding predictable upgrade windows for change-control, and legal pushback on indemnity/maintenance language. Current packaging mixes license + ad-hoc support quotes which lead to long negotiation cycles and inconsistent economics.
proposed_solution: Introduce three canonical entitlement bundles (Foundation, ManagedOps, CompliancePlus) and two upgrade cadence options (Managed Auto-Upgrades with monthly security backports; Controlled Scheduled-Upgrades with quarterly major roll windows). Each bundle defines license fee bands (per-node or per-GPU) and a complementary ops subscription that can be purchased as an add-on or included with enterprise commits.
experiments: Pilot A: Offer Foundation + Controlled Scheduled-Upgrades to 3 existing mid-market customers; price as flat annual license + optional ops subscription at 12% of license value.
Pilot B: Offer ManagedOps bundle (ops included) to 2 enterprise accounts under a 24-month commitment with 10% discount on license and guaranteed monthly security patches.
A/B pricing: test per-GPU pricing vs per-node flat bands for similar workload profiles and measure procurement velocity and total contract value.
Security QA path: run tailored SQ template with two pilot customers to capture common redlines and produce pre-approved Contract Appendix for legal.
acceptance_criteria: Documented bundle definitions with SKU mapping and clear entitlement matrix (features, support response times, upgrade policy).
Pilot contracts signed by at least 4 pilot customers using new constructs and legal-approved appendix included.
Sales enablement kit (pricing cheat sheet, negotiation playbook, T&Cs appendix) delivered and validated in two sales motions.
Security questionnaire common redlines captured and a recommended answers playbook published.
Telemetry to measure upgrade failure rate and post-upgrade incident rate for managed vs controlled cohorts instrumented.
success_metrics: Reduction in average RFP negotiation cycles for on-prem deals from X to <=60 days (baseline to be measured).
Conversion rate of pilot offers to closed deals >= 50% across pilots.
Average ARR per deal uplift of >=8% when ops subscription is included.
Mean time to remediate critical vulnerabilities under ManagedOps <= 48 hours.
Customer satisfaction (post-upgrade survey) >= 4.0/5 for managed cohort.
dependencies: Legal: pre-approved appendix and indemnity language
Security: finalize SQ template answers and required attestations
Engineering: implement upgrade toggle and per-customer upgrade windows in control plane
Billing: SKU and contract amendment flow for ops subscription
Sales Ops: CRM SKUs and quoting templates
risks: Customers may prefer no-op upgrade responsibility; ops subscription adoption could be lower than expected.
Engineering scope to support per-customer upgrade windows may require >2 sprints of work causing timeline slips.
Legal redlines on maintenance/indemnity could increase contract negotiation time if appendix is insufficient.
If pricing bands are misaligned, we risk revenue cannibalization from current bespoke quotes.
notes: Do not reuse the existing 'flexband' naming; aim for clear commercial language to procurement teams.
Target initial pilots in North America with customers on Dedicated or Private plans who have requested predictable maintenance windows.
Coordinate with Customer Success to select pilot accounts with historical willingness to pay for managed services.
